resources.string: Earth → Moon. A quiet first voyage to our nearest celestial neighbor.
Earth → Venus → Mercury. Follow the real inner planets toward the Sun.
Earth → Mars. From our blue home to the red planet.
Earth → Mars → Saturn → Uranus. A red world, golden rings and a pale blue ice giant.
Earth → Jupiter → Pluto. Follow the encounter order of New Horizons.
Earth → Jupiter → Saturn → Uranus → Neptune. Follow the planetary encounter order of Voyager 2.
Real solar-system worlds. Scale and time are condensed for your focus session.
Earth → Proxima Centauri b. Visit the radial-velocity planet around our nearest stellar neighbor.
Earth → TRAPPIST-1 e → f → g. Follow three observed planets outward through one compact system.
Earth → LHS 1140 b. An atmospheric research target investigated with JWST.
Earth → TOI-700 e → d. Two small planets in the same system, ordered from inner to outer orbit.
Earth → 55 Cancri e. A remote flyby of an extremely hot super-Earth studied through thermal emission.
Radial-velocity detection. Surface and atmosphere remain unconfirmed; the view is an artist interpretation.
Transit observations confirm these planets. Surface water and habitability are not established; scenery is interpretive.
JWST studies test atmospheric and water-rich scenarios. An ocean is not confirmed; the icy view is one interpretation.
TESS transit detections. Habitable-zone location does not establish water or life; surfaces are artist interpretations.
JWST thermal spectroscopy motivates an extremely hot world with a possible secondary atmosphere. Surface detail is interpretive.
